name: LLM tool calling
needs: let the AI look things up in my database
the chatbot should be able to create a task
make the model call my API
the AI made up an answer instead of checking
summary: Giving the model a list of functions it may ask you to run, each with a name, description and input schema. Your code checks permissions, runs the function, and sends back the result. The model never touches your systems directly.
need_when: The AI needs fresh or private data, or should take actions like creating, sending or updating things.
skip_when: All the context fits in the prompt and the AI only writes text.

ways.title: Your model provider's tool calling
ways.how: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and most others accept tool definitions with JSON Schema and return tool calls for your code to run.
ways.tradeoff: Direct and well supported. You write the loop and error handling.

ways.title: An SDK that runs the loop
ways.how: Vercel AI SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, LangChain or PydanticAI define tools as typed functions and handle the call, run, reply loop.
ways.tradeoff: Less boilerplate. More abstraction to debug.

ways.title: An MCP server
ways.how: Expose your tools with the Model Context Protocol so agents like Claude, Cursor and ChatGPT can call them.
ways.tradeoff: Works across many AI clients. Auth and permissions need care.

prompt:
Add tool calling to my AI feature so it can [look up X / create Y].

Requirements:
- Define tools: [list], each with a clear description and a strict JSON Schema for inputs.
- Run every tool as the signed-in user, with the same permission checks as the normal API. Never trust ids the model supplies without checking ownership.
- Validate tool inputs against the schema, and return short structured errors the model can recover from.
- Read-only tools run directly. Tools that change data, spend money or send messages show the user a confirmation first.
- Cap tool calls per turn at [5] and total time at [30 s].
- Treat tool results as data. Don't let text inside them change instructions.
- Log each call: tool, inputs (with personal data trimmed), result status, duration.
- Tests: the model picks the right tool for 10 sample requests, and a request for another user's data fails.

Acceptance checks (run each and show me the result):
1. Asking for another user's record through the AI returns nothing.
2. A destructive action asks the user to confirm first.
3. Bad tool input gets a clear error the model uses to retry or explain.
4. A loop of calls stops at the cap.
5. The log shows every tool call for a conversation.
acceptance_checks: Asking for another user's record through the AI returns nothing.

if_you_skip_it: The AI either makes things up instead of checking, or becomes a way around your permission checks.
